items.note: Three studies give people LLM-generated cross-domain analogies in a problem-reformulation task and report helpfulness ratings and changes in formulations; the abstract names no no-AI comparison condition and no creativity score, so the full text must show whether a comparison exists.

Undergraduate design course compares an AI-assisted path (DeepSeek) with a traditional path on design quality (72.43 vs 65.60) with SEM cognitive-load mediation; the assignment method and sample size are not stated.

Controlled comparison of three human-machine division-of-labor modes (manual, AI-assisted, AI full-process) over 80 print-ad tasks and 240 samples, scored on quality, brand fit and creative depth plus a 300-person audience survey; the number of designers is not stated.

User study with 24 novice designers compares ConceptVis (LLM with interactive knowledge graph) with a chat-based LLM interface for concept generation, reporting concept diversity and performance; an AI-versus-AI-configuration contrast with fewer than 50 participants. Journal version of a DETC 2024 paper.

Between-subjects experiment (N=247) crossing timing and labeling of AI suggestions with a no-AI control in two-round ideation on plastic pollution, with rated creativity and anchoring outcomes; the abstract does not say 'random'. Crossref also holds a duplicate DOI 10.24963/ijcai.2024/1142.

Within-subjects study (N=16 teachers) compares LitLinker with a plain LLM chatbot for ideating interdisciplinary teaching contexts, scoring integration depth of ideas and workload; order randomization not stated. arXiv 2502.16097 is the same work.

Controlled experiment with 36 participants in pairs compares a digital collaboration tool with and without AI features, rating idea novelty and appropriateness (AI pairs more novel, less appropriate, not significant).

Counterbalanced experiment compares human-only, human-plus-multi-agent-LLM and agent-only brainstorming on general and domain-specific topics, with originality scores and embedding-based semantic dispersion; sample size not stated (abstract from Semantic Scholar).

Wizard-of-Oz study with 20 mechanical designers using generative design tools with or without metacognitive support agents; agent-supported users made more feasible designs. The outcome is feasibility rather than creativity, and the GenAI tool is present in both arms.

Seven students generated ideas individually or in groups with AI tools, and the study looks at participants' views and outputs; the abstract shows no no-AI or alternative-AI condition, so this may be out as a descriptive study without an AI contrast.
